title: Shopify Theme Harness Agent-Tools Error Codes
description: Stable agent-readable codes for the Shopify agent-tool server documented in harness/config/agent-tools.example.json. The agent should match a server response by status + message regex (compiled with the supplied flags) and quote the resulting code in section-result.openIssues so reviewers can triage without rereading server logs.

matchSyntax.note: messageMatch is a JavaScript regex source string. Compile with `new RegExp(messageMatch, flags)` where `flags` defaults to "i" for case-insensitive matching.

codes.summary: Request did not include an Authorization: Bearer <export-token> header.
codes.remediation: Set the env var named by toolServer.auth.tokenEnv (typically SHOPIFY_AGENT_TOOL_TOKEN) to the plaintext export token issued by the server, then re-run.

codes.summary: Bearer token's sha256 does not match any row in the server's ExportToken table. Common cause: agent set the token env var to the tokenHash column rather than the plaintext value the server printed at issuance.
codes.remediation: Have a maintainer issue (or rotate) an export token via the server admin path and copy the printed plaintext into the env var. Do not paste the tokenHash column from the database.

codes.messageMatch: approve the updated shopify app scopes
codes.summary: Server rejected fetching shop context because the bound store has not approved the Shopify app scopes the server requires.
codes.remediation: Have a Shopify admin reinstall or reauthorize the app on the bound store. The agent should not retry until the maintainer confirms scope approval; section work that does not need shop context can proceed.

codes.messageMatch: multipart sync upload (manifest is invalid|is missing the manifest field)
codes.summary: The multipart upload's `manifest` form field was missing or did not parse to {assets: [...]} with a fileField pointing at each attached file.
codes.remediation: Send the manifest as a plain text form field (no `;type=application/json` content-type override), with shape {"assets":[{"assetId":"...","filename":"...","mimeType":"...","alt":"...","fileField":"file_<n>"}]}, then attach each file under the same fileField name.

codes.messageMatch: a request field is not a valid JSON as declared by its Content-Type
codes.summary: Fastify's multipart parser tried to JSON-parse the manifest field because the client labelled it as application/json. The current server expects the manifest as a plain text field.
codes.remediation: Drop the `;type=application/json` (or any explicit content-type) on the manifest form field; pass it as plain text. Example: `curl -F 'manifest={...}' -F 'file_desktop=@./asset.png;type=image/png' ...`.

codes.summary: One of the attached files exceeded the server's MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (default 15 MB).
codes.remediation: Re-export the asset at a smaller size, split into multiple uploads, or have the maintainer raise MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES on the server.

codes.summary: The agent hit an undocumented endpoint, often by guessing a path the server does not implement (e.g. /files/upload, /shop, /tools).
codes.remediation: Use only the paths declared by toolServer.routes in harness/config/agent-tools.json; do not invent paths. If a needed route is missing, treat it as a server upgrade ask and report it as a blocker rather than guessing.
